source.title: Understanding Generalization in the Interpolation Regime using the Rate Function
source.authors: Andrés R. Masegosa; Luis A. Ortega

record.file_problem: none noted; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps the size of nested convolutional networks and measures train and test performance, directly testing model-size double descent in a new experimental setup.
record.gate_note: Section 5 and Figure 6 report the study's own size-sweep results. Test NLL and test accuracy are tabulated separately; train accuracy is noted alongside each NLL row to locate interpolation. The reported PAC-Chernoff bound is not itself test error and is not recorded as a row. Cited findings from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own model-size sweep of nested LeNet-like CNNs on CIFAR10 and reports test NLL and test accuracy against train accuracy (Fig. 6). That directly bears on V1, in a new setting: no label noise, NLL as the main measure, and a train-loss stopping rule.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors present Fig. 6 as an illustration of double descent in test loss (NLL): loss worsens up to a critical region near interpolation, then improves with more parameters. Their PAC-Chernoff bound tracks this curve and is tight for interpolators. They attribute the second descent to larger interpolators being smoother (higher rate functions, Fig. 7), and argue this is plausibly because larger networks capture invariances. They do not discuss the test-accuracy curve, which shows no peak.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a nested LeNet-like convolutional network on CIFAR10 and reports test NLL as well as test accuracy; the study presents this as an illustration of double descent, not an explicit replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported pattern differs by metric: test NLL shows a pronounced peak near interpolation, while test accuracy does not show a comparable peak in its implied error.

fits_no_version.finding: Estimated rate functions (smoothness) decrease with size before interpolation and increase with size after it (Fig. 7). The PAC-Chernoff bound itself traces a double-descent shape and is tight for interpolators (Fig. 6 table, Bound column).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distribution-dependent rate-function smoothness of interpolators increases with size past the interpolation threshold, tracking the second descent in test loss.

record.problems: The model-size evidence is limited to one nested convolutional-network family on CIFAR10. Test NLL and test accuracy show materially different curve shapes, and no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No reported test-error outcomes from the Section 5, Figure 6 size sweep were left out.

untested.parts: Only one CNN family on CIFAR10, without label noise, and with no 0-1 error peak. Other architectures, datasets and noise levels are not tested.
No effective-complexity measure used to predict the peak across axes. The rate function is examined only along the size axis.
No label-noise manipulation, no multiple descent, no tuned-regularization sweep across sizes.
No re-expression of the curve against an effective parameter count.

missing.what: The full sweep of models (k from 0.2 to 4.9 in steps of 0.1, roughly 48 models) is plotted in Fig. 6, but only 10 are tabulated. rows_left_out wrongly says nothing was left out. The exact peak location and smoothness of the full curve can be read only from the plot.
missing.locator: Figure 6 plot and caption ('Only a few of the total models are shown'); Appendix A.1 Figure 6

missing.what: Inconsistent size range: Section 5 says 4k–1161k, Appendix A says 7k–1.2M. Training stopped at train loss 0.01 or after two epochs without improvement, not trained to convergence.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The double descent here is visible only in NLL. Test 0-1 error improves almost monotonically, which is consistent with the originals' observation that peaks are weak without label noise. That is why the accuracy rows get limits_scope, not challenges. No uncertainty or seeds are reported. The experiment is an illustration for a theory paper.

versions.untested_parts: Only one nested convolutional-network family on CIFAR10 is tested; broader model and dataset generality is not tested.
No test-error sweep over training epochs.
No sweep over training-set sample size near the interpolation threshold.
No comparison across model classes; the experiment sweeps sizes within one convolutional-network family.
The study does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across size, epochs, and sample size.
The study does not test noise dependence, multiple or triple descent, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
The study does not re-express the curve against an effective parameter count or test whether that turns it into an ordinary U-shape.

relationships.reason: Test NLL falls 1.56→1.17, peaks at 2.28 where train accuracy first hits 100%, then falls to 1.72 (r1–r10).
